title: Fighting erupts along the Nagorno-Karabakh line of contact, starting the 44-day war
body:
Fighting began on the morning of 27 September 2020 along the line of contact left by the First Nagorno-Karabakh War and lasted 44 days, ending with the ceasefire that took effect on 10 November 2020. The opening action was an Azerbaijani ground offensive supported by artillery, drones and loitering munitions, with the most intense clashes in the less mountainous southern districts. Azerbaijan struck infrastructure from the first day, including rocket artillery and cluster munitions against Stepanakert and a missile strike on a bridge on the Lachin corridor. Its drones destroyed Armenian air defences.

Both Armenia and Azerbaijan declared martial law. Azerbaijan restricted internet access on 27 September, imposed a curfew in several cities from 28 September and ordered partial mobilisation the same day. Armenia banned men over 18 in the mobilisation reserve from leaving the country on 28 September. On the sixth day Armenian and Artsakh forces fired the first of four ballistic missile attacks on Ganja, nominally aimed at the military part of its airport but hitting residential areas.

Casualty figures came from the combatants. Azerbaijan reported 2,906 servicemen killed, while Armenia and Artsakh reported 3,825. Civilian deaths were reported as about 100 Azerbaijanis and 85 Armenians, and around 100,000 Armenians were displaced. Russia, France and the United States brokered three ceasefires that failed to halt the fighting before Russia helped negotiate the agreement of November 2020.
